audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged in the packet: the content layer never names a single Gragas ability. It says 'body-slam', 'Q-pool', 'Cask', 'W damage reduction' throughout.
audit.why: The real names are Happy Hour (P), Barrel Roll (Q), Drunken Rage (W), Body Slam (E) and Explosive Cask (R). A loading-screen coach that cannot name the ability about to kill you is not usable at the moment it matters.
audit.corrected: Named all five across spikes, whys, wants, early, mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four places credit Gragas with a 'Q-pool' that heals him: whys[0] 'your ranged auto trade with his Q-pool sustain', whys[1] 'Q-pool sustain', early 'a clean chunk his Q-pool can't fully heal yet', mid 'Q-pools the rest back'.
audit.why: Gragas has no pool ability. Barrel Roll is a rolled cask that detonates; his healing is Happy Hour, the passive, which heals him periodically whenever he uses a skill. That changes the anti-heal read completely — his sustain is gated on casting anything at all, not on one spell Mel can bait out.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour heals him off any ability cast; there is no pool.
sources: champ-data/_kits/gragas.json (P: 'Gragas periodically heals upon using a skill'; Q: 'rolls his cask to a location')

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text says 'his E knocks you toward turret and his R can flip you under it'.
audit.why: Body Slam stuns — 'dealing damage to all nearby enemy units and stunning them'. It carries no displacement. The knockback belongs to Explosive Cask alone. For a champion whose only escape is spacing, knowing that the charge locks her in place rather than moving her is what decides whether Rebuttal or Flash is the right answer.
audit.corrected: Body Slam charges in and stuns; Explosive Cask is the displacement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears in either layer. wants.foe[0] frames the lane as 'Body-slam onto you the instant your Solar Snare is on cooldown', implying his engage outpaces her root.
audit.why: It is the other way round. Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12; Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9. Mel's root returns three seconds before his engage does at every rank, so spending E on his charge is correct and she is never the one caught waiting. Explosive Cask is 100s at rank 1 and Barrel Roll 10s.
audit.corrected: Body Slam 14s at rank 1 against an 11s Solar Snare — spend the root on his engage and yours is back first.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] says to hold Rebuttal 'to wall and reflect his Q barrel', and late says 'eating his barrel with your wall is the only way you survive his engage'.
audit.why: Barrel Roll carries only a slow flag in the kit — it is a rolled and detonated cask, not a projectile fired at Mel, so it is not what the reflect clause returns. Rebuttal's other two clauses are what actually save her here: it prevents damage outright and grants movement speed, which is exactly the answer to a Body Slam engage.
audit.corrected: Hold Rebuttal for the Body Slam engage — the damage prevention and the move speed are what carry you out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W: prevents damage, grants movement speed)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.trading and report[3].t both say a spent Rebuttal is gone 'for twenty seconds'.

edits.before: Your only real window is levels 2-3. Get Q + E first and the moment Gragas steps up to last-hit, land Solar Snare's root and dump Radiant Volley on him — that's a clean chunk his Q-pool can't fully heal yet. After that, respect his body-slam: his E closes your range in one dash and he's tankier than you with W damage reduction up. Don't trade autos into him, don't push past river, and hold Rebuttal — it's your only disengage if he commits.
edits.after: Your only real window is levels 2-3. Get Q + E first and the moment Gragas steps up to last-hit, land Solar Snare's root and dump Radiant Volley on him — that's a clean chunk Happy Hour can't fully heal back yet. After that, respect Body Slam: it charges your range down in one dash and stuns, and Drunken Rage has him taking reduced damage. Don't trade autos into him, don't push past river, and hold Rebuttal — it's your only disengage if he commits.

edits.before: Once Gragas has W and his E-into-R online, the lane tilts to him. He soaks your Radiant Volley with W's damage reduction and Q-pools the rest back, so your poke stops pricing him out. At 6 he can body-slam in and Cask you under turret — one Solar Snare on cooldown is all he needs. Only commit when your E root is up AND you have Rebuttal banked. If you don't have both, just farm at max range and accept you can't kill him.
edits.after: Once Gragas has Drunken Rage and Body Slam into Explosive Cask online, the lane tilts to him. He soaks Radiant Volley behind damage reduction while Happy Hour heals the rest back, so your poke stops pricing him out. At 6 he can charge in and Cask you under turret. But Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 against Solar Snare's 11s — spend the root on his engage and yours is back before his is.

edits.before: This stays his lane. Gragas' E-Q-AA burst and Cask outrange the safety your dash-less, one-CC kit depends on, and his W damage reduction blunts the Overwhelm stacks you'd need to execute him. Your passive scales, but he's a durable AP bruiser who only needs one E body-slam to delete your spacing. Group with your team, never sidelane alone into him, and keep Rebuttal for the moment he flips — eating his barrel with your wall is the only way you survive his engage.
edits.after: This stays his lane. Body Slam into Explosive Cask outranges the safety your dash-less, one-CC kit depends on, and Drunken Rage's damage reduction blunts the Overwhelm stacks you'd need to execute him. Your passive scales, but he's a durable AP bruiser who only needs one charge to delete your spacing. Group with your team, never sidelane alone into him, and keep Rebuttal for the moment he commits — it blanks the engage damage and the move speed carries you out.

notes: The packet's defect for this matchup was that it never names a Gragas ability; underneath that were two invented mechanics. Four places gave him a 'Q-pool' that heals him — Gragas has no pool, and his sustain is Happy Hour firing off any skill cast, which is a completely different anti-heal read. And spikes[1] said Body Slam knocks Mel toward turret; it stuns, and the displacement is Explosive Cask. The most useful new fact is the cooldown relationship the entry had backwards: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 against Solar Snare's 11s, so Mel's root returns before his engage at every rank, which turns 'he charges the moment your E is down' into 'spend E on the charge, you get it back first'. Also retargeted the Rebuttal advice: the entry told her to reflect Barrel Roll, which carries only a slow flag and is a rolled cask rather than a projectile fired at her — the damage prevention and move speed are the clauses that matter against his engage. Full-layer verdict fields remain uncorrectable through the applier (shared boilerplate, exactly-once rule).
